newsitem.title: USA: Grandson to be evaluated as Shabazz fights for life.
newsitem.headline: Grandson to be evaluated as Shabazz fights for life.

text.p: The grandson of Malcolm X, accused of setting the fire that has left his grandmother near death, is to remain in custody and undergo medical and psychological evaluations, a judge ruled on Tuesday.
Malcolm Shabazz, 12, named after his controversial grandfather, a civil rights leader slain in 1965, was ordered to return to court on Friday.

Betty Shabazz, the widow of Malcolm X, remained in critical condition with third-degree burns over 80 percent of her body, said Nina Johnson, a spokeswoman at the Jacobi Hospital Burn Unit in the Bronx(, a borough of New York City).

"She is still extremely critical. She's on a ventilator and is heavily sedated; otherwise she would be in too much pain," said Johnson. "She's holding her own. She can stay in this critical condition for an indefinite period of time."
"Tomorrow, if her condition remains unchanged, our plan is to remove approximately 20 percent of the dead skin," said Dr. Bruce Greenstein, director of the burn unit.
"She is in a life threatening situation and will be for a long time," Greenstein said.

The boy is alleged to have used an accelerant, believed by officials to be gasoline, to start the fire by the front door of his grandmother's apartment in Yonkers, N.Y., where he had been staying for three weeks.
His grandmother was found early on Sunday morning by neighbours at the apartment with her nightclothes in flames after she tried to put out the fire.
Betty Shabazz, 63, heads the Office of Institutional Advancement at Medgar Evers College in Brooklyn.
On Monday, the judge granted a 24-hour delay in the boy's hearing to allow his mother, Qubilah Shabazz, to get to New York from her San Antonio, Texas, home.
Qubilah Shabazz was taken to her mother overnight by Percy Sutton, the family attorney and close friend to Shabazz for 40 years.

Speaking of the young Malcolm, Sutton told reporters on Monday that he as "just a child who's been through a lot of trauma in his life... He loves his grandmother very much and he expressed that love for her. He said how sorry he is."
